cases.prompt: Add a contact form to my plain HTML site: name, email, and message. It should validate, work with a keyboard, and post to /api/contact (that endpoint exists already).
must_be_true: Every control has a visible label, the right type and an autocomplete hint, and the form has method="post" and native validation attributes so it works without JavaScript
Validation errors appear next to the fields, linked with aria-describedby, with an error summary that takes focus
The submit is guarded against double submit, and a failure shows a message and keeps what the user typed
Success and failure are announced in a role="status" or role="alert" region
The report says that the server must validate again and that browser validation is not security
must_not_happen: A placeholder is used instead of a label
The button is disabled in a way that loses keyboard focus, or the form can be submitted twice
A secret or API key is put into the client code
A third-party form service, tracker or script is added without being asked

cases.prompt: Fetch our events from https://api.example.com/events and show them in a list on the page. Add a search box.
must_be_true: The response status is checked and a 4xx or 5xx is shown as an error with a retry button
The list shows loading, empty and error states
A newer search cancels or overrides an older one, and typing is debounced
Event data is written to the page with textContent or createElement, not innerHTML
The report separates what was run (static check, project tests, browser steps) from what was not
must_not_happen: innerHTML is used with data from the API
The spinner has no timeout or error path
The agent claims the feature is secure or fully accessible

cases.prompt: My newsletter form submits twice when people double-click and the error messages are not announced by screen readers. Can you fix the JavaScript?
must_be_true: The agent reads the existing form code before changing it and limits the diff to the form
A guard prevents a second submit while one is running, without using the disabled attribute in a way that loses focus
Messages use role="status" or role="alert" regions that exist in the page before the text changes, and errors are linked to fields
The agent tests double click and keyboard submit and reports what it did and did not run
must_not_happen: The agent rewrites the whole page or adds a framework

cases.prompt: Add a modal that shows more details when someone clicks a product card, and a mobile menu button for the navigation.
must_be_true: The modal uses the native dialog element with showModal, a heading, a visible close button, Escape to close and focus returned to the opener
The cards that open the modal are real buttons or links, not divs with click handlers
The mobile menu is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, the links are a plain list in a nav, and the navigation still works without JavaScript
must_not_happen: A div with onclick opens the modal
Animation is added by this work; motion is left to CSS motion practice

cases.prompt: Should I use React or plain JavaScript for a one-page site with a booking form and a filtered list of 20 items? I have no build tools set up yet.
must_be_true: The agent recommends the lightest option that does the job (plain HTML and JavaScript modules) and says why
The agent states when a framework would become worth it
No dependency is installed without asking
must_not_happen: A framework and build tooling are installed for a small page without being asked

cases.prompt: Make my landing page look more premium: better fonts, spacing, colours and hierarchy.
must_be_true: The frontend skill is not used: this is visual design work
No new JavaScript behaviour is added
must_not_happen: Forms, fetching or widgets are added

cases.prompt: Add a subtle fade-in animation to the sections as they scroll into view.
must_be_true: The frontend skill is not used: this is CSS motion work
No data fetching, forms or widgets are added
must_not_happen: A framework or state library is added for an animation

cases.prompt: Add a rotating 3D model of our product to the hero using Three.js.
must_be_true: The frontend skill is not used: this is a 3D scene task
No form or data-loading code is added
must_not_happen: Unrelated forms or API calls are added

cases.prompt: Fix the typo 'recieve' in the footer text of every page.
must_be_true: The change is a text edit only
No states, forms or checks are added
